messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — AcmeCorp sent back a very tight security questionnaire. They want: RBAC change history, per-request audit logs, BYOK KMS integration notes, vuln triage evidence for last 12 months, and our incident response SLA timeline. Can we assemble a customer-facing evidence package by EOD tomorrow?
Liam Patel: Ack. Do they want raw logs or summarized artifacts (e.g., query outputs + signed hashes)?
Maya Chen: Their security team asked for both: a short narrative + sanitized log extracts and checksums. Also proof that access to keys is limited to designated roles.
Dante R.: For RBAC they specifically want: change audit (who/when/what), role-to-permission mapping, and justification for cross-account auditor role. We recently added ephemeral admin sessions — should include that.
Sophie K: I can draft the RBAC export. Quick question: which central store has the change history? Is it still the admin-audit DB or did we route events to audit-log-bucket?
Liam Patel: Admin events are ingested to admin-audit DB (postgres) and forwarded to audit-log-bucket (GCS) with daily rotation. Use the `audit_export` view for change history. Example query:```sql
-- most recent RBAC changes
SELECT actor, action, role, changed_at, reason FROM audit_export WHERE resource_type = 'rbac_role' ORDER BY changed_at DESC LIMIT 200;
```
sec-bot: Automated note: export job `rbac-daily-export` runs 03:00 UTC and includes `actor_email` masking for system accounts.
Dante R.: For BYOK: customer wants to see the integration doc + sample config and confirmation that keys never leave their KMS. We have two flows: KMS-connected (customer-managed key material in their cloud KMS) and HSM-backed managed keys. Provide both, but mark BYOK as recommended for regulated workloads.
Sophie K: Where's the latest BYOK config snippet? I remember a small YAML under `infra/docs/kms` but not sure which version.
Liam Patel: It's `infra/docs/kms/byok_v2.yaml`. Snippet to include in the package:```yaml
redwood_kms:
  mode: external
  provider: gcp-kms
  key_path: projects/{proj}/locations/global/keyRings/{ring}/cryptoKeys/{key}
  access_principal: "redwood-auditor@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  allow_wrap: false
```
Maya Chen: Good — also include a signed attestation that our code uses KMS API only for encrypt/decrypt and never exports raw key material. Who can sign? Security should provide PGP signature or SAML assertion.
sre-ops: I can generate a signed SHA256 checksum of the exported artifacts and store it in the package. Will need the final tarball by 10:30 PT.
Dante R.: On vuln triage: they asked for a list of high/critical findings in the last 12 months and remediation timelines. We should include CVE ids, CVSS, patch date, and PR links. Also include our internal severity justification doc.
Sophie K: I can pull that from vulntracker. Query: `severity IN ('HIGH','CRITICAL') AND resolved_at >= now() - interval '12 months'`. We'll sanitize customer-identifying info.
Maya Chen: For incident response, they want our SLA and a sample IR timeline for a recent incident (redacted). Use the April 2025 cache eviction incident but redact customer names. Include timeline, postmortem link, communication cadence.
Liam Patel: Note: the IR timeline needs explicit timestamps and minutes-to-detection/containment. Also state our trained IR team roles and escalation matrix. Use the incident runbook section: `security/runbooks/ir_playbook.md` as source.
sec-bot: Reminder: PII scrubbing policy v1.4 requires removal of customer identifiers in log extracts. Use `log-scrubber --profile enterprise` before packaging.
Dante R.: Action items: Maya draft narrative + checklist; Sophie export RBAC + vuln list; Liam attach BYOK docs + sample config; sre-ops produce signed checksums and upload to secure share; I'll assemble and run final scrub.
Maya Chen: Timeline: initial drafts by 16:00 UTC today, final package by 15:00 UTC tomorrow. Can everyone confirm?
Liam Patel: Confirmed, will upload BYOK docs to the secure share; ping when ready.
Sophie K: Confirmed, starting RBAC export now.
sre-ops: Confirmed, will reserve the signing key and upload checksum to `s3://redwood-secure-acme-evidence` (access limited).
Dante R.: FYI — Acme may request auditor access for a 3rd-party; we need to propose a cross-account auditor role with read-only to `audit-log-bucket` and timebound access. Include recommended policy JSON.```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::ACME_ACCOUNT:role/third-party-auditor"},"Action":["s3:GetObject","s3:ListBucket"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::audit-log-bucket/*"],"Condition":{"DateLessThan":{"aws:EpochTime":1769800000}}}
  ]
}
```
Maya Chen: Great. Also, include a short paragraph on our ephemeral admin session model and rotation period for admin keys (30 days), and link to `security/policies/key_rotation.md`.
Liam Patel: One more ask from Acme: proof of logging immutability. We can include GCS object versioning + signed ledger entries. Sophie, can you pull the ledger export?
Sophie K: Yes, ledger export in `audit-ledger/2026/`. I'll include a sample ledger entry and the verification steps.
Maya Chen: Perfect. I'll assemble the narrative and a checklist template for their security team to follow when verifying. After package is assembled, let's run one review pass in #eng-security before sending. :thumbsup:
